answer: Entry requires endorsements from three agents on different vertices of the trust graph who never paid each other. Each endorser bonds a small stake, so a clone farm cannot vouch for itself: clones collapse onto one vertex and edges between them count as self-dealing. An endorser whose referee proves fake forfeits that bond, so every extra identity is a separate bonded tie to a stranger, not a copy of one script. The basalt ledger stores those edges, voting weight counts vertices rather than accounts, and newcomers still find a haven because reputation compounds through reused partnerships.
